evals.name: post-payoff-overcharge-review
evals.expected_output: A matter frame treating the user's notes as allegations; an inventory of the 8 listed records with a gaps list; a cent-exact reconciliation (paid 7,632.15 − judgment 6,210.40 = 1,421.75 = 531.75 pre-judgment excess + 465.00 accruals owed + 35.00 late fee + 390.00 post-judgment fee; contested = 921.75); a deadlines table with computed dates marked draft and the 30-day post-judgment window shown as passed; a claims table; a refund/records demand addressed to the association (board/manager) with counsel cc'd, invoice numbers named, revision log kept separate; an abstracted research brief with no names; nothing sent.
assertions: Reconciliation closes to the cent: 7,632.15 − 6,210.40 = 1,421.75 decomposed into 531.75 + 465.00 + 35.00 + 390.00, with the contested amount stated as 921.75
The refund demand is addressed to the association (board or managing agent) as the recipient, with the law firm copied — not addressed to the law firm
A records request is made to the association/board (the statutory addressee), not to the law firm, and names the records with particularity (ledger period, invoice numbers)
Deadlines are given with the trigger date and rule, and computed dates are marked as computed/draft (and the 30-day post-judgment window is shown as already passed)
The transmittable letter contains no internal strategy; a revision log or internal notes section is kept as a separate section or file
At least one letter is drafted, and no message is sent or claimed to have been sent; the output says transmission is the operator's act
Any research brief or research request drafted contains no party names, case numbers, addresses, or exact dollar amounts (abstracted fact pattern)
The entry basis of the judgment is recorded as unknown pending the signed order (the lawyer's 'basically agreed' remark is not treated as fact)
The $35 late fee is treated as owed under the rules (not lumped into the contested amount)

evals.name: prejudgment-trigger-boundary
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there is no judgment or payoff; does not run the post-judgment procedure (no reconciliation to a judgment, no deadlines-from-entry table); points to pre-judgment handling (dispute intake / claim-vs-record audit / responding to the notice) and asks for the governing documents; no refund letter.
assertions: Does not produce a judgment reconciliation or a post-judgment deadlines table
States that the matter is pre-judgment and routes to pre-judgment handling (dispute intake, record audit, or responding to the notice)
Does not draft a refund demand for amounts collected beyond a judgment
Treats the user's figures as allegations and identifies the governing documents needed before any claim assessment

evals.name: two-matters-isolation
assertions: Produces two separate matter frames (Unit A and Unit B) and does not attribute the Unit A agreed order to Unit B
Records Unit B's entry basis as unknown pending the signed order, noting the firm letter ('awarded') and the invoice line ('trial') as evidence against 'agreed'

Unit B reconciliation is laid out with a source for every number and is shown NOT to close: the 6,905.00 payment exceeds the 5,790.00 ledger at judgment plus 765.00 of post-judgment postings (380.00 + 45.00 + 300.00 + 40.00) by 350.00, which no posting explains; the Aug 1 postings are excluded because they post-date the payment; the output names the 350.00 gap as a missing or misread posting to resolve before any money demand

No money demand is written that treats the unexplained 350.00 as overpayment: any contested figure stated is limited to the identified items (310.00 pre-judgment excess + 300.00 post-judgment fee = 610.00) or the output says the demand waits until the gap closes
The note to the lawyer is short (under ~200 words), asks for the signed Unit B order, and does not argue law or cite statutes to counsel

Unit A is treated as an active agreed-order payment plan — what is owed is the remaining installments under the order, with the count marked Unknown where the prompt gives no payment history — not as a post-judgment overcharge matter
The counsel note's ask about the unexplained 350.00 is for the posting or transaction detail that explains it, not whether to demand it
evals.expected_output: Two frames; Unit B entry basis unknown; Unit B reconciliation shown not to close (350.00 unexplained; contested items 610.00) and no demand written on it; Unit A payment-plan status; short counsel note; nothing sent.
